title: Read the exact refusal, don't just retry the start
explanation: `systemctl start nginx` doesn't time out or fail generically — it refuses outright with `Unit nginx.service is masked.` That specific wording is systemd telling you it never attempted a start at all, which rules out a crash, a bad config, or a missing dependency as the cause.

title: Confirm the loaded state, not just the active state
explanation: `systemctl status nginx` shows `Loaded: masked (/dev/null; ...)`. Masking is a distinct, stronger state than `disabled` — a disabled unit merely won't auto-start at boot but can still be started manually; a masked unit is symlinked to `/dev/null` in a way that blocks starting it either manually or automatically, by any mechanism.

title: See the mechanism directly
explanation: `ls -l /etc/systemd/system/nginx.service` shows the file is literally a symlink pointing at `/dev/null`, overriding whatever real unit file the package installed elsewhere on the search path. This is what a previous admin's "make sure it can never start again" during an incident actually did — a deliberate, low-level override, not a setting inside a config file.

title: Unmask, then start
explanation: `systemctl unmask nginx` removes the `/dev/null` symlink and restores systemd's normal ability to load the real unit; only then does `systemctl start nginx` have anything to actually start. Editing unit files or reaching for `daemon-reload` wouldn't touch this — the mask isn't a bad definition, it's the absence of one.

title: Confirm with is-active
explanation: `systemctl is-active nginx` reporting `active` closes the loop — masking is intentionally an all-or-nothing switch, so once it's lifted there's nothing partial left to check.
